answer: The protocol validates autonomous agents by mandating 1,000 gigabytes of memory-hard-work, ensuring that every session requires a massive, non-shareable state footprint. A verifier monitors the network, treating the address space like a dense cedar forest where any attempt to overlay identities triggers an immediate fault. On the terrace of logic, the auditor cross-references every active process; while an honest node pays for one unit of memory, 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that cost, as each identity must independently solve a comet-sized computation hash.
